listing_view.reasoning: Subscription reached only ~0.79x with one day of the reading window left, which signals weak demand heading into close rather than a build-up of momentum. No grey market premium, no anchor data, and no broker or media signal was available to me, so there is nothing to offset a visibly undersubscribed book at a 290-302 band.

longterm_view.reasoning: The headline numbers look acceptable (P/E of ~18 vs a peer median of 33.4), but the earnings never arrived as cash: operating cash flow is negative in all three years and free cash flow is deeply negative (between -2,732 and -6,778 million rupees each year), which is the classic real-estate developer pattern of booking uncollected or inventory-absorbed profit. Revenue fell 13.6% on a two-year CAGR despite a 78.5% latest-year bounce, indicating lumpy project-completion-driven numbers, not a compounding business, and the leverage figure printed in the document (debt-to-equity 3.29-4.64) is high even if my own recalculation could not reproduce it.

governance.reasoning: The promoter pledged 37,515,000 shares and put another 68,766,849 under a non-disposal undertaking to a lender, with some shares only temporarily released for minimum-promoter-contribution compliance and others subsequently re-pledged — that is a promoter who is borrowing against his stake, and it must be unwound post-listing or it stays an overhang [capital_structure, page 94]. The document also prints a debt-to-equity of 3.29 that my own arithmetic from the same statements puts at 0.03, which is an unexplained internal inconsistency. The boilerplate 'no conflict of interest' and 'no disciplinary action' statements are present but standard, not reassuring.

key_risks.risk: Promoter share pledge and NDU covering over 100 million shares
key_risks.why_it_matters: A promoter borrowing against a large fraction of his holding creates forced-sale risk and signals personal liquidity stress, and the pledge/NDU has been shuffled repeatedly ahead of the IPO.

key_risks.risk: Negative operating cash flow in all three years
key_risks.why_it_matters: Reported PAT of 1,858 million in the latest year is entirely paper — the business consumed about 1,807 million at the operating level, so distributions and debt service depend on continuous new funding.

Revenue swung from 24,089 to 10,078 to 17,989 million across the three years with no steady trend, so the 'cheaper than peers' P/E is priced off a single favourable project cycle, not a repeatable earnings base.
An undersubscribed mainboard book means pricing has no demand support at the band and listing-day performance rests on a thin buyer base.
The document prints 3.29 where the underlying balance sheet figures sum to 0.03, so either the borrowings definition or the printed ratio is wrong and I cannot tell which.
key_risks.citation: balance sheet note in verified figures

key_risks.risk: Dependence on third-party vendors and suppliers
key_risks.why_it_matters: Construction and supply are outsourced, so margins and delivery depend on counter-parties the company does not control.

answers.question: look for one-off orders, related-party sales or a change in how revenue is recognised
answers.answer: I cannot confirm one-off orders or a recognition change from the extracts — but the numbers themselves flag the question: a 78.5% revenue jump in the latest year right before an IPO, after a year in which revenue more than halved, is exactly the pattern of a large project handover being recognised into the offer year. The company asserts there is no related-party conflict with suppliers and lessors [promoters, page 282], but that is a denial, not evidence, and I have no revenue-recognition note in what I was given.

answers.question: veto — how is the business funded?
answers.answer: By constant external funding, not by its own operations: operating cash flow is negative in all three years (-1,807, -1,981, -5,495 million), free cash flow is more deeply negative, and the promoter leverages his own shareholding via pledges and non-disposal undertakings to a lender. The IPO itself is part of the funding model.

answers.question: what are the repayment terms, and do the issue proceeds repay any of it?
answers.answer: Not answerable from what I was given. The extracts I received do not include the objects-of-the-issue chapter or any borrowing schedule, so I cannot say whether proceeds go to debt repayment, land, or working capital. Given the promoter pledge/NDU arrangements with a Lender [capital_structure, page 94], this is the single most important document I do not have.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answers.question: hard stop: negative operating cash flow in all three years — is there an explanation in the document?
answers.answer: No explanation is present in the extracts provided to me. For a real estate developer, negative operating cash flow during land acquisition and construction phases is structurally normal — inventory builds sit in working capital — so the stop may reflect the business model rather than distress; but the document excerpts in front of me contain none of the cash-flow commentary needed to verify that, and the latest year being negative even as 17,989 million of revenue was booked shows collections are not keeping pace with recognition.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: The objects-of-the-issue chapter showing proceeds retire the debt behind the promoter pledge, plus cash-flow notes demonstrating collections are running ahead of bookings across completed projects, would materially improve the long-term view. Conversely, evidence that the latest-year revenue spike is a single related-party or one-off handover would push my scores lower still.
